title: Training Load and Injury Risk — Building Athletes, Not Breaking Them

hook.en: Athletes rarely get injured by training itself, but by sudden jumps in it. Learn how to read load, plan progression and spot the early signs of overload.
hook.ur: Khilari training se shayad hi zakhmi hote hain, balkay us mein achanak izafe se. Load parhna, progression ka plan banana aur overload ki shuruati nishaniyan pehchanna seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll define training load, explain why sudden increases raise injury risk while a steady, high chronic load protects, and apply a simple monitoring and progression plan with rest and recovery.
goal.ur: End tak aap training load ki tareef karenge, samjhayenge ke achanak izafa chot ka khatra kyun barhata hai jabke musalsal, zyada chronic load bachata hai, aur aaram aur recovery ke saath saada monitoring aur progression ka plan lagayenge.

text.en: **Training load** is how much work the body does: distance, minutes, sets, or how hard it **felt** (the session rating of perceived exertion multiplied by minutes). Tissues adapt to load that rises **gradually**. Injury risk goes up when the recent load is much higher than what the body is used to, for example a runner who doubles the weekly distance. Athletes who train steadily at a **high chronic load** tend to be **more robust**.
text.ur: **Training load** yeh hai ke jism kitna kaam karta hai: faasla, minutes, sets, ya woh kitna **mehsoos** hua (session ki rating of perceived exertion ko minutes se zarb). Tissues us load se dhal jate hain jo **aahista** barhta hai. Chot ka khatra tab barhta hai jab haal ka load us se bohat zyada ho jis ka jism aadi hai, maslan daudne wala jo haftay ki doori doguni kar de. Jo khilari **zyada chronic load** par musalsal training karte hain woh **zyada mazboot** hote hain.

text.en: Think of the body as a **bank account for fitness**. Steady deposits (training) build a large balance (chronic load) that can cover bigger days. A sudden large withdrawal, such as three hard matches in a week, with a small balance, makes the account overdrawn, and that is when tissues break.
text.ur: Jism ko **fitness ka bank account** samjhein. Musalsal jama (training) bara balance (chronic load) banati hai jo bari mehnat sambhal sakta hai. Chhote balance ke saath achanak bara nikalna, maslan haftay mein teen sakht matches, account ko overdrawn kar deta hai, aur tab tissues tootte hain.

steps.title: Measure what the athlete does
steps.detail: Record each session's time and how hard it felt (a one to ten scale), and note sleep, soreness and mood. Simple tools in a notebook or phone work well. || Khilari kya karta hai naapein

steps.title: Compare recent and usual load
steps.detail: Compare this week with the average of the past four weeks. Large and fast jumps, or a long break followed by a hard return, deserve a closer look. || Haal aur aam load ka muqabla karein

steps.title: Progress gradually
steps.detail: Raise load in small steps, change one thing at a time (distance, speed or frequency) and plan easier weeks. There is no magic number; ten percent is a rough guide, not a rule. || Aahista barhayein

steps.title: Watch for warning signs
steps.detail: Persistent pain that builds or lingers, poor sleep, low mood, heavy legs and falling performance may all show overload. Reduce load early, not after an injury. || Warning signs dekhein

question.en: Which athlete is at greatest risk of overuse injury?
question.ur: Kaun sa khilari overuse chot ke sab se zyada khatre mein hai?

text.en: One who rests a lot and trains lightly
text.ur: Jo bohat aaram kare aur halka train kare

feedback.en: Low load does not cause overload.

text.en: One who trains steadily at a high load for months
text.ur: Jo mahino musalsal zyada load par train kare

feedback.ur: Musalsal zyada load mazbooti paida karta hai.

text.en: One who doubles weekly running distance after a break
text.ur: Jo break ke baad haftay ki daur ki doori doguni kar de

feedback.en: Yes — a sudden large jump in load exceeds what tissues are used to.
feedback.ur: Haan — load mein achanak bara izafa us se zyada hai jis ke tissues aadi hain.

rows.en: The average of the past four weeks or more
rows.ur: Pichle chaar ya zyada haftay ka ausat

rows.en: How much the body did recently
rows.ur: Jism ne haal mein kitna kiya

rows.en: What the body is prepared for
rows.ur: Jism kis ke liye taiyar hai

rows.en: Rises when much higher than the chronic load
rows.ur: Chronic load se bohat zyada hone par barhta hai

rows.en: Higher chronic load tends to protect
rows.ur: Zyada chronic load aam taur par bachata hai

text.en: **Steady up, no spikes.** Raise load in small, regular steps and watch the early signs. Rest is part of training, not a failure of it.
text.ur: **Musalsal oopar, izafa nahi.** Load chhote, baqaida qadmon mein barhayein aur shuruati nishaniyan dekhein. Aaram training ka hissa hai, us ki nakami nahi.

text.en: **Treating a ratio as a law.** Ratios of recent to usual load are helpful guides, but they are not exact and do not predict injury in any one person. Use them to start a conversation, together with how the athlete feels and the context.
text.ur: **Ratio ko qanoon samajhna.** Haal aur aam load ke ratios madadgar rehnumai hain, magar durust nahi aur kisi ek shakhs ki chot ki peshgoi nahi karte. Inhein baat shuru karne ke liye istemal karein, khilari ke mehsoos karne aur halat ke saath.

question.en: A runner's weekly distance goes from 20 to 45 kilometres in two weeks and her shins hurt. What is the best response?
question.ur: Daudne wali ki haftay ki doori do haftay mein 20 se 45 kilometre ho gayi aur pindliyan dukh rahi hain. Behtareen jawab kya hai?

text.ur: Bardasht banane ke liye dobara barhayein

feedback.en: A further spike raises the risk.

text.en: Stop all exercise for six months
Reduce load now, explain the build-up, and restart with a gradual plan
text.ur: Abhi load kam karein, izafa samjhayein aur aahista plan se dobara shuru karein

feedback.en: Yes — the spike probably explains the pain; early action prevents a stress injury.
feedback.ur: Haan — izafa shayad dard ki wajah hai; jaldi kaarwai stress injury se bachati hai.

question.en: Which sign should prompt a medical review?
question.ur: Kaun si nishani medical review ki wajah honi chahiye?

text.en: General tiredness the day after a hard session
text.ur: Sakht session ke agle din aam thakan

text.en: Mild muscle soreness for two days

feedback.en: That is normal after new training.
feedback.ur: Naye training ke baad normal hai.

text.en: Pain at one bone point that is worse at night with a rising load
text.ur: Ek haddi ke point par dard jo raat ko zyada ho aur load ke saath barhe

feedback.en: Yes — this can be a stress fracture and needs imaging.
feedback.ur: Haan — yeh stress fracture ho sakta hai aur imaging chahiye.

text.en: **Plan the week with the athlete.** Agree easy, moderate and hard days, protect a rest day and keep a note of sleep and mood. After illness or a break, return at about half the previous load and build over two to four weeks. Explain that the plan is a map, not a rule, and adjust it with how the athlete feels.
text.ur: **Haftay ka plan khilari ke saath banayein.** Aasan, darmiyane aur sakht din tay karein, aik aaram ka din mehfooz rakhein aur neend aur mood ka note rakhein. Bimari ya break ke baad pichle load ke takreeban aadhay par wapas aayein aur do se chaar haftay mein barhayein. Samjhayein ke plan naqsha hai, qanoon nahi, aur khilari ke mehsoos karne ke mutabiq badlein.

question.en: Why can a high chronic load protect against injury?
question.ur: Zyada chronic load chot se kyun bacha sakta hai?

answer.en: Tissues, such as tendon and bone, adapt to repeated, gradually increasing load by becoming stronger and more resilient. An athlete with a well-built base can cope with demanding days, whereas the same hard day is risky for an athlete who has done little.
answer.ur: Tissues, maslan tendon aur haddi, baar baar aur aahista barhte load par mazboot aur lachakdar ho kar dhal jate hain. Achhi bunyad wala khilari mushkil dinon ko sambhal leta hai, jabke wohi sakht din kam training karne wale khilari ke liye khatarnak hai.

beats.patient: A cricket fast bowler bowls 30 overs a week in training, but in a tournament bowls 90 overs in a week. In the second match, he feels low back pain that grows.
beats.assessment: A threefold jump in bowling load is the likely driver; the pain may be an early overload or a stress reaction of the back.
beats.treatment: Reduce bowling, check for bone tenderness and refer for imaging if present, build a gradual plan with strength work and agree on a workload limit with the coach.
beats.reassess: After rest and a graded return, he bowls 50 overs a week without pain.

text.en: **Refer for medical review** for pain at a single bone point that is worse at night or with rest, pain that keeps rising despite less load, swelling or deformity after a fall, chest pain, fainting, unusual breathlessness, repeated heavy headaches after a head knock, or signs of low energy availability such as missed periods, repeated illness and fatigue.
text.ur: **Medical review ke liye refer karein** ek haddi ke point par dard jo raat ko ya aaram mein zyada ho, load kam karne ke bawajood barhta dard, girne ke baad sujan ya bad-shakli, seene ka dard, behoshi, ghair mamooli saans ki tangi, sar par chot ke baad baar baar bhari sar dard, ya kam energy ki nishaniyan, maslan mahwari ka band hona, baar baar bimari aur thakan.

summary.en: Training load is how much work the body does; tissues adapt to load that rises gradually, and sudden jumps raise injury risk.
summary.ur: Training load woh kaam hai jo jism karta hai; tissues us load se dhalte hain jo aahista barhta hai, aur achanak izafe chot ka khatra barhate hain.

summary.en: Measure sessions, compare recent with usual load, progress in small steps and treat ratios as guides, not laws.
summary.ur: Sessions naapein, haal ka aam load se muqabla karein, chhote qadmon mein barhayein aur ratios ko rehnumai samjhein, qanoon nahi.

summary.en: Watch for warning signs and act early; refer bone-point night pain, falls with deformity, chest pain and signs of low energy availability.
summary.ur: Warning signs dekhein aur jaldi kaarwai karein; haddi ke point ka raat ka dard, bad-shakli ke saath girna, seene ka dard aur kam energy ki nishaniyon par refer karein.

back.en: The amount of work the body does, often time multiplied by how hard it felt.
back.ur: Jism ka kiya hua kaam, aksar waqt ko is se zarb ke woh kitna sakht laga.

front.ur: Chot ka khatra kya barhata hai?

back.en: A sudden large rise in load compared with what the body is used to.
back.ur: Load mein achanak bara izafa jis ka jism aadi nahi.

front.ur: Chot se kya bacha sakta hai?

back.en: A steady, high chronic load built gradually.
back.ur: Aahista banaya gaya musalsal, zyada chronic load.

back.en: A rough guide for weekly increases, not an exact rule.
back.ur: Haftay ke izafe ki aam rehnumai, durust usool nahi.

note.en: Dose, progress and monitor exercise with RPE.
note.ur: RPE ke saath exercise ki dosage, progression aur monitoring.
Tissues load se kaise dhalte hain.
